name: Alphatec Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: Alphatec Holdings (ATEC) is a spine-focused medical technology company offering an integrated procedural ecosystem: lateral and posterior approach systems (including PTP), implants and biologics, SafeOp neuromonitoring, EOS low-dose 3D imaging with AI-driven alignment measures, and the Valence navigation and robotics platform. FY2025 revenue was $764M (+25%). Q3 2026 revenue rose 13% to $221M with ~20% case growth, but management cut FY2026 revenue guidance to ~$862M (from $882M) on lower biologics attachment, weaker procedure volumes and an international supply constraint, and the stock fell roughly 36% to ~$7. Chairman and CEO Pat Miles has led the company since 2017.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Since Pat Miles arrived in 2017 the company has been rebuilt into a spine-only procedural platform, growing revenue from $144.9M in FY2020 to $764.2M in FY2025 (~39% CAGR) through the PTP lateral approach, the EOS imaging acquisition and SafeOp neuromonitoring [2][4]. It stops short of 3 because the platform remains unprofitable and the Q3 2026 guidance cut shows revenue per case falling ~5% [1]. AI Deployment (2/2): AI-based automated alignment measures with 3D reconstruction against normative values have shipped on EOS since 2024, and EOS Insight has reached 15-20% of the installed base faster than expected [2]. Market Share (2/2): ATEC remains the fastest share gainer in U.S. spine, with Q3 2026 case volumes up ~20% versus a low-single-digit market [1]. Product Pipeline (2/2): Valence navigation/robotics plus recent FDA clearances for intraoperative alignment and the Contour 3D automated rod bender give named next-generation products, which Miles positions as the 'operating system' for spine procedures [2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D of $76.3M equals ~10% of FY2025 revenue, above typical orthopedic/spine device peers [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): ATEC's purpose of revolutionizing the approach to spine surgery through clinical distinction is specific and has visibly shaped strategy — the company exited non-spine distractions, built surgeon-centric procedural systems and integrated imaging, neuromonitoring and navigation into one ecosystem [2]. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive charitable or community program surfaced in research. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data found. Insider Buying (0/2): CEO Pat Miles sold 100,000 shares on December 1, 2025 at ~$22.11 (~$2.2M) and no offsetting insider buying was identified [3].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on growth-stock metrics (10 weight units). D/E of 2,788% scores 0.0 (equity is nearly exhausted by accumulated losses) [5]. ROE of -308% scores 0.0 at 2x weight [5]. Revenue growth YoY of 12.6% scores 1.0, consistent with Q3 2026 revenue +13% [1][5]. 5-year revenue CAGR of 39.5% (FY2020 $144.9M to FY2025 $764.2M, derived from reported statements) scores 1.0 at 2x weight [4]. Forward P/E of 12.8 scores 1.0 [5]. Profit margin of -10.3% scores 0.0 [5]. Provider-reported forward PEG of 0.48 scores 1.0 at 2x weight; note it rests on forward EPS estimates that predate the Q3 guidance cut [5]. Weighted sum 6.0 / 10 x 10 = 6. Liquidity: $7.31 x 2.97M shares = ~$21.7M daily — passes the $1M floor.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): ATEC sells physical implants, surgical access systems, imaging hardware and navigation/robotics used in the operating room under FDA regulation — AI cannot substitute for these products, and the searches surfaced no analyst concern about AI displacement [1][2]. AI is instead embedded as an enabler: automated EOS alignment measures and Valence software deepen surgeon lock-in. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI-enabled features are shipping and EOS Insight has 15-20% installed-base penetration, but the company does not disclose quantified AI-attributable revenue, so the tiebreaker point is not awarded [2].

infinite_game.summary: ATEC shows real infinite-game traits: a focused cause (reinventing spine surgery), a decade-long willingness to fund R&D and surgeon education through deep losses, and a genuine reinvention of a near-distressed company after 2017 [2][4]. It scores 6/10 because its competitive language is about taking share from incumbents, the CEO has been a seller of stock, and the Q3 2026 guidance cut — the second downward revision this year — exposes how dependent the story is on hitting near-term numbers [1][3].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Revolutionizing the approach to spine surgery' is distinctive and visibly drives product decisions — integrating EOS imaging, SafeOp neuromonitoring and Valence navigation so that surgeons can plan, execute and confirm alignment in one ecosystem [2]. It has not yet been tested by a leadership transition or multi-decade consistency, which keeps it at 2.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership has been stable under Pat Miles since 2017 and the company has scaled revenue more than 5x without visible cultural crises [2][4]. No employee-engagement, tenure or Glassdoor data surfaced, and a plaintiff-firm investigation following Q1 2026 results adds some pressure, so the score stays at adequate [6].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): ATEC's public messaging centers on share capture from larger incumbents such as Medtronic and Globus, framed around case-volume gains rather than learning from rivals' strengths — a finite, win-the-market framing [1][2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Alphatec effectively reinvented itself after 2017, shedding its international business and rebuilding as a U.S. spine-only procedural innovator, then expanding from implants into imaging (EOS) and navigation/robotics (Valence) — a transformation that took revenue from $144.9M in 2020 to $764.2M in 2025 [2][4].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management sustained heavy R&D (~10% of revenue) and surgeon-education investment through years of losses, including net losses of $143-$187M annually from 2021-2025, to build a long-term platform [4]. Offsetting this, the CEO sold ~$2.2M of stock in December 2025 and the company declined to give 2027 guidance after the Q3 2026 cut [1][3].

investment_thesis: ATEC is the fastest-growing scaled spine company, with revenue compounding ~39% annually from FY2020 to FY2025 and Q3 2026 case volumes still up ~20% [1][4]. The integrated ecosystem — PTP lateral access, SafeOp neuromonitoring, EOS imaging with AI-automated alignment, and Valence navigation/robotics with new FDA clearances for intraoperative alignment and the Contour 3D rod bender — creates surgeon switching costs that peers selling standalone implants lack [2]. Adjusted EBITDA rose 46% year-over-year to $38.3M in Q3 2026, showing operating leverage, and after a ~36% post-earnings drop the shares trade at ~$7.31, a forward P/E of 12.8 and a provider PEG of 0.48 [1][5]. The Inspire Impact Score of +48 (ALIGNED) with no negative attributions supports faith-based suitability.
thesis_continued: The bear case is that growth is getting more expensive and the balance sheet is thin. FY2026 revenue guidance was cut to ~$862M from $882M (and from ~$890M in January), with revenue per case down ~5% on lower biologics attachment, softer procedure volumes and an international supply constraint, and management declined to give 2027 guidance [1][2]. GAAP profit margin is still -10.3%, ROE is -308%, and D/E of 2,788% reflects equity nearly erased by cumulative losses, leaving limited cushion [5]. The CEO sold ~$2.2M of stock at ~$22 in December 2025, and a plaintiff firm opened a securities-claims investigation after Q1 2026 results — risks that could intensify after the Q3 miss [3][6].
key_catalysts: Valence navigation/robotics commercial ramp following FDA clearances for intraoperative alignment and Contour 3D automated rod bending, increasing per-procedure revenue capture [2]
EOS Insight adoption beyond the current 15-20% of the installed base, pulling through implant and biologics share with EOS-equipped surgeons [2]
Continued adjusted EBITDA leverage (Q3 2026 +46% to $38.3M) moving the company toward sustained positive free cash flow [1]
key_risks: Revenue-per-case erosion (~-5% in Q3 2026) from lower biologics attachment and pricing, which drove the FY2026 guidance cut to ~$862M and a ~36% stock decline [1]
Balance-sheet fragility: D/E of 2,788% and ROE of -308% leave little equity cushion if losses persist or refinancing is needed [5]
Securities-litigation and credibility risk after repeated guidance reductions in 2026, compounded by CEO share sales [3][6]
